robot.name: Booster K1
robot.status_notes: Official product page and distributor pages show 'Buy now' and list prices; Booster Robotics claims launch equals shipment. Press release says Geek Edition USD 5,999 with limited-time USD 4,999 before Nov 11. Generation Robots lists from €9,000 incl VAT; Robotics Center lists from $11,998. No home consumer sale found; intended for education/research.

height.notes: Official product page lists approximately 95 cm standing height.

weight.notes: Official product page lists approximately 19.5 kg.

payload.notes: No payload specification found in reviewed sources.

runtime.notes: Battery life varies by edition. Official page lists 70 min for 5 Ah models and 20 min for 2 Ah Geek. Generation Robots indicates up to 1h20 in practical use.

battery.notes: Battery capacity specified per edition. Charging time ≤ 1 hour per Generation Robots.

degrees_of_freedom.notes: 6 per leg, 4 per arm, 2 head. Total DoF 22.

walking_speed.notes: Official product page spec. Robotics Center lists walk speed ±0.5 m/s; conflict kept in researcher_notes.

hands.description: No dedicated hand specification found. Arms have 4 DoF each; no hand DoF, force feedback, or dexterous manipulation details published.

items: Tactile sensors (listed by Generation Robots, not explicitly on official product page)

compute.description: 48 TOPS (Geek, Qualcomm QCS8550), 117 TOPS (Education, NVIDIA Jetson Orin NX 8GB), 200 TOPS (Professional, NVIDIA Jetson Orin AGX 32GB) depending on version.

actuators.description: Max peak torque 60 N·m, dual encoders, torque-controlled joints.

availability.notes: Starting price $4,999 was a limited-time offer before Nov 11, 2025; list price for Geek is $5,999. Generation Robots lists from €9,000 incl VAT; Robotics Center lists from $11,998. Prices vary by region and version.

manipulation_dexterity.summary: Arms have 4 DoF each and Generation Robots lists tactile sensors, but no hand dexterity, grasping, or manipulation demos are described in the sources. The product page mentions Agents including dance and martial arts, but without specific manipulation tasks.
caveats: No hand DoF published.
No manipulation demos, success rates, or independent benchmarks found.
Tactile sensors listed only by distributor.

autonomy_task_execution.summary: Official product page claims the Soccer Agent 'tracks, chases, and shoots—all on its own', and fall recovery is described as autonomous. The RoboCup 2025 KidSize league win (platform used by winning team) provides some external validation of autonomous soccer behavior, but no autonomous manipulation or other task execution is documented.
caveats: Autonomy claims are company-asserted.
RoboCup win is attributed to the team using the platform, not directly to K1 autonomous capabilities.
No intervention logs or independent audits.

mobility_whole_body_control.summary: Official specs list 2 m/s walking speed and 1.5 rad/s turning. Product page claims active balance recovery and auto get-up. Competition success (RoboCup KidSize) suggests agility, but no independent mobility measurements or disturbance tests are published.
caveats: Official 2 m/s spec conflicts with Robotics Center listing ±0.5 m/s.
Balance recovery is a company claim without video or independent verification in sources.
No fall rate or recovery success rate published.

perception_scene_understanding.summary: Integrated sensors include stereo depth camera, 9-axis IMU, microphone array, speaker, and tactile sensors (distributor). The official page mentions visual perception and voice interaction, but no specific perception tasks, benchmarks, or scene understanding demos are provided.
caveats: No object recognition, tracking, or SLAM results published.
Tactile sensors not confirmed on official page.

human_interaction.summary: Official page claims real-time voice conversations in Chinese/English, multiple personas, and customizable conversation settings. Handheld controller and app control are described.
caveats: No measured conversational accuracy or user studies.
Voice interaction is a company claim.

endurance_reliability.summary: Battery life 20–70 minutes depending on edition; charging time ≤ 1 hour. Company press release claims 30 hours of 500N impact testing and 100 hours of real-machine operation. Generation Robots mentions CE/FCC certification.
caveats: Durability testing is company-reported without test protocol.
Battery life is spec, not independently measured.
CE/FCC listed by distributor; full certification details not provided.

human_environment_fit.summary: Compact size (95 cm, 19.5 kg) with carrying handle, designed for classrooms, labs, and competitions. Safety features include soft/hard emergency stop, automatic stop on fall, low battery and overheat warnings.
caveats: No full safety certification beyond CE/FCC listing.
Intended for research/education, not home use.

deployment_commercial_proof.summary: Purchasable from official store and distributors (Generation Robots, Robotics Center). Company press release claims over 700 units shipped globally (company-wide, not K1-specific) serving 200+ clients, 20+ countries, 70+ universities. Competition wins provide proof of field use.
caveats: 700+ units is company-wide across all Booster products, not K1-specific.
No revenue or model breakdown provided.
No named customer deployment with output metrics.

accessibility_value.summary: Strong evidence of accessibility: public pricing from $4,999 (limited launch offer) to $5,999 list for Geek, €9,000 incl VAT from Generation Robots, $11,998 from Robotics Center. SDK support for Python and C++, ROS2 compatibility, open simulation resources.
caveats: Prices vary by region and version.
$4,999 was a limited-time offer.
No subscription or additional software costs detailed.

researcher_notes.short_verdict_for_arena: Booster K1 is a compact, purchasable research humanoid with strong accessibility (from ~$5k) and competition validation (RoboCup KidSize 2025 winner platform). However, most capability claims are company-asserted, and video sources lack transcripts, limiting independent verification.
strongest_positive_evidence: Public pricing and buy-now availability from multiple distributors.
RoboCup 2025 KidSize league win using K1 as platform.
Official specs: 22 DoF, up to 200 TOPS, 2 m/s claimed walking speed.
weakest_or_missing_evidence: No hand dexterity or manipulation demos.
No independent autonomy verification or intervention logs.
Walking speed conflict between official and distributor specs.
conflicting_claims: Walking speed: official 2 m/s vs Robotics Center ±0.5 m/s.
Price: $4,999 limited-time vs $5,999 list vs €9,000 (EU) vs $11,998 (Robotics Center).
Battery life: official 70 min (5Ah) vs Generation Robots 'up to 1h20'.
do_not_overclaim: Do not credit T1 championship to K1; that is Booster T1.
Do not treat 700+ units as K1-specific.
Do not treat video titles as evidence of capabilities without transcripts.
Do not describe manipulation capabilities beyond 4-DoF arms and tactile sensor listing.

arena_prompt_summary.one_paragraph_summary: Booster K1 is a compact (95 cm, 19.5 kg) bipedal humanoid from Booster Robotics (China), positioned as an entry-level research/education platform with 22 DoF, up to 200 TOPS compute, stereo depth camera, voice interaction, and official walking speed 2 m/s. It is purchasable from distributors from about $4,999 (limited launch offer) to €9,000 or $11,998 depending on region. Its strongest validation is being the platform of the winning team in RoboCup 2025 KidSize league. However, most capability claims (autonomous soccer, balance recovery, durability) are company-asserted without independent verification, and video demos lack transcripts. No hand dexterity, payload, or per-model shipment data is available.
strongest_evidence: Public purchase availability and pricing (multiple sources).
RoboCup 2025 KidSize win using K1 platform.
Official specs: 22 DoF, 2 m/s, up to 200 TOPS.
known_do_not_credit: Manipulation capabilities beyond listed arms/tactile sensors.
